findings.title: Unstable hash() cache key with 60s stale allowlist returns wrong counts
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py the cache key is built with Python hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). Python hash() is salted per-process, so different workers produce different keys and never share cache, and collisions are possible. Worse, the cached value is only allowlist eligibility cached for 60 seconds. If the allowlist changes, queries for up to 60s use the stale decision and return upsampled sum(sample_weight) instead of count() or vice versa. invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but never called anywhere, so there is no invalidation. The new endpoint tests reuse the same org and project ids with different mocked allowlists, so the second test will hit the first test's cached True and get wrong results.

findings.title: Upsampling check uses outer dataset and request instead of scoped query
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py _get_event_stats receives scoped_dataset and query as arguments but calls is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request) using the outer closure dataset and the original request. The dashboard-split factory calls the same function with split_dataset=discover and rewritten queries like (query) AND !event.type:transaction. Because the check ignores scoped_dataset and the query argument and instead inspects request.GET, split queries are evaluated against the wrong dataset and wrong query string, so errors routed to discover will not be upsampled and transactions routed elsewhere may be.

findings.title: Error detection only matches event.type:error substring
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py _is_error_focused_query returns True only if the lowercased request query string contains event.type:error. It misses the queries this endpoint itself generates for the discover split, e.g. (query) AND !event.type:transaction, misses empty or default discover queries that include errors, and misses event.type:default/error variants. It also false-positives on substring matches like message:event.type:error. Consequence is discover error traffic silently uses raw count() instead of upsampled_count() or vice versa, producing inconsistent charts.

findings.title: upsampled_count assumes sample_weight exists and truncates with toInt64
findings.body: In src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py upsampled_count is defined as toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no coalesce, ifNotFinite, or null handling. The helper comments admit it assumes sample_weight exists for all events in allowlisted projects. Older events, non-sampled events, or transactions in a mixed discover query will have NULL/missing sample_weight, so sum can be NULL/0 and counts collapse to 0. toInt64 also truncates fractional weights like 1/0.3=3.33, systematically undercounting. The result is wrong chart values instead of falling back to count().

findings.title: Transform only handles bare count() and discards original alias
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites columns where lowered stripped value equals count(), always emitting upsampled_count() as count. It drops any original alias like COUNT() as my_count, does not handle yAxis forms with aliases, equations, or count_if/count_unique, and leaves other count-like aggregates unconverted. Consequence is broken aliases for top-events/orderby that expect the original name and dashboards mixing upsampled and raw counts in the same response.

findings.title: Test helper silently overwrites sample_rate with unvalidated value
findings.body: In src/sentry/testutils/factories.py _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling wraps all access in bare try/except pass, checks if client_sample_rate truthy, then does float(client_sample_rate) with another swallowed exception and unconditionally assigns normalized_data[sample_rate]. It does not validate 0 < rate <= 1, so 0, negative, >1, or string values either silently pass or silently fail, and it overwrites any legitimate existing sample_rate. This creates invalid test fixtures that do not represent production validation and can mask missing server-side checks.

findings.title: Cache invalidation helper is dead code
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py invalidate_upsampling_cache deletes the eligibility key, but nothing in the pull request calls it when issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist changes. Combined with the 60 second TTL, allowlist removals keep returning upsampled counts and additions keep returning raw counts until expiry. The function gives a false impression of consistency while the stale-read window remains.
